page: Vultr vx1-g-4c-16g-240s is a general-purpose virtual server belonging to the VX1 Cloud Compute family. It features an x86_64 AMD EPYC processor with 4 dedicated vCPUs, derived from 2 physical cores with 2 threads per core. The CPU operates at a clock speed of 2.0 GHz and includes a 32 MB L3 cache. The system is equipped with 16.0 GB of system memory, providing 4.0 GB of RAM per core, and includes 240 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. No GPU accelerators are included in this configuration.

Benchmark data indicates strong single-core capabilities, with stress-ng single-core CPU performance, single-threaded gzip compression, and single-threaded bzip3 decompression all placing in the top tier. Conversely, multi-threaded scaling presents some limitations, as evidenced by weak multi-core Geekbench scores and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression results. Memory bandwidth is moderate, with read-only small block cached bandwidth at 440.06 GB/sec and uncached large block write bandwidth at 41.27 GB/sec.

This server offers a balanced resource profile for general-purpose workloads, combining dedicated AMD EPYC processing with fast NVMe storage. It is qualitatively cost-efficient for workloads that rely heavily on single-threaded execution speed or require a steady, non-burstable allocation of CPU and memory. Appropriate workloads include static web serving, lightweight database operations, text processing, and software compilation. It is less suited for heavy multi-threaded parallel processing or large-scale language model inference.
